subject: PaxonHealth - elevated 5xx/429s and timeouts (urgent)
messages:
From: John Liu <john.liu@paxonhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <ops@paxonhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: High 5xx/429 and timeouts impacting live traffic - immediate help needed

Markus,

We started seeing a sustained spike in 5xx and 429 responses from Redwood starting ~2026-03-15T07:55:00Z. Our payment flows are timing out and customer-facing errors are increasing. This is affecting two production endpoints (create_session and authorize_payment). Key observations from our side:
- 5xx rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~8% between 07:55-08:30 UTC
- 429s clustered around 08:05 UTC corresponding to a playback loop in our retryer
- Some requests show multi-second tail latencies and client retries -> amplification

We have a support call in 20 minutes but wanted to loop you in by email and share traces (link below) and a minimal stack trace snippet. Please escalate — our SLAs are at risk and we need an immediate mitigation plan or rollback guidance.

Trace link: https://paxon.splunk.com/trace/abc123
Snippet: 504 gateway timeout at infer/v1/generate after 2500ms

Thanks,
John Liu
SRE Lead, PaxonHealth

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, John Liu <john.liu@paxonhealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 and timeouts impacting live traffic - immediate help needed

Quick triage summary from infra: we see a concurrency burst against the r3-serving pool tied to a customer-side retry pattern. Timeline and findings:
- 07:28 UTC: rolling kernel optimization (kv-cache eviction heuristics) rolled to 30% of r3 nodes (internal job id job-789)
- 07:55 UTC: traffic surge from Paxon (multiple identical request IDs from client retries) -> KV cache misses amplify latency
- 08:03 UTC: autoscaler attempted to add instances but hit a transient quota stall for that AZ (rate of scale-up limited); scaling delay ~90s
- 08:10-08:30 UTC: increased 5xx (502/504) and 429 from fronting proxies as queues filled

Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Rolled back kernel change to previous stable on r3-serving (completed 08:22 UTC)
- Tightened per-tenant queue limits and temporarily increased per-tenant concurrency cap for Paxon to reduce rejects (08:28 UTC)
- Bumped autoscaler buffer for r3 pool and requested quota increase with infra team

Suggested short-term customer-facing mitigations for Paxon:
- Apply a client-side exponential backoff with jitter and a max retry cap (we can provide a suggested retry policy)
- Temporarily reduce retry count on create_session/authorize_payment to 1

Next steps for internal follow-up: runbook updates for cache-eviction rollouts, add pre-deploy blast-radius checks for kernel heuristics, and an alert for scaling stalls by AZ. Linking runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-paxon-incident

—Dev (oncall)
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: SRE Team <ops@paxonhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: John Liu <john.liu@paxonhealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 and timeouts impacting live traffic - immediate help needed

Thanks — we confirmed on our side that a client-side change deployed at ~07:40 UTC increased aggressive retries (defaulted to 5 retries with no jitter). We’ve pushed a hotfix to throttle retries downstream and reduced client retry to 1 while we stabilize. Observations:
- Error spike aligns with job-789 rollout window
- After rollback + client throttle we see error rate drop to ~0.9% by 09:00 UTC

Two asks from Paxon's SRE/ops leadership:
1) We need an incident timeline and a commit-point for the kernel heuristic change (for our postmortem and compliance)
2) Paxon would like to discuss prorated SLA credits given outage impact to customers (they are escalating internally)

On the call you mentioned tuning alerts and SLOs — can you share the proposed alert rule changes and an interim SLO safety window?

—Paxon SRE Team
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: SRE Team <ops@paxonhealth.com>, John Liu <john.liu@paxonhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 11:43:00 -07:00
Subject: PaxonHealth incident recap, actions, and ask list

Team — summary and actions after our triage and stabilization:

What happened (TL;DR):
- A kernel eviction heuristic change (job-789) rolled to a subset of r3-serving nodes shortly before a customer-side retry policy change. The combination produced KV cache churn, longer tail latencies, and retry amplification leading to 5xx/429 spikes.

Immediate timeline highlights:
- 07:28 UTC: job-789 rollout started
- 07:40 UTC: Paxon client retry change deployed
- 07:55 UTC: error rates begin rising
- 08:22 UTC: rollback of job-789 completed
- 08:28 UTC: temporary per-tenant concurrency bump and queue caps applied
- 09:00 UTC: error rate back to ~0.9% from peak ~8%

Customer-facing mitigations we executed:
- Rollback of the kernel change
- Temporary routing and concurrency adjustments for Paxon
- Recommended client retry settings delivered to Paxon (doc attached)

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Infra: Add a pre- and post-deploy smoke check for cache eviction heuristics; BLOCK deploy without healthy smoke by default (owner: dev_patel; ETA 2026-03-23)
- Observability: New alert for per-AZ scaling stalls and a per-tenant queue-fill warning with 5-min and 1-min thresholds (owner: hannah_schmitt; ETA 2026-03-18)
- Product/CS: Draft SLA credit proposal and customer comms (owner: stephanie_nguyen; ETA 2026-03-18)
- Platform: Reserve short-term dedicated capacity buffer for Paxon during their high-traffic window (owner: markus_klein; ETA 2026-03-19)
- Docs: Update runbook and add a specific retry-amplification appendix (owner: dev_patel; ETA 2026-03-20)

Links and attachments:
- Incident timeline PDF and raw logs attached (incident-timeline.pdf, paxon_error_log.zip)
- Internal ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-2567
- Runbook draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-paxon-incident

We appreciate the fast coordination from Paxon SREs. Stephanie will follow up on credits and exec comms. We'll schedule a postmortem review with Paxon next week; I'll send calendar invites.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
